name: Tracer AI-writing tells
regexFlavour: ECMAScript (JavaScript). No lookbehind/backreferences, so patterns also work in Rust’s regex crate if you convert flags to inline form: g → drop, i → (?i), m → (?m), u → default. One rule (rhetorical-reveal) uses a lookahead; swap (?=\s|$) for (?:\s|$) in Rust.

scoring.weights: 1 = weak hint, 2 = mild, 3 = moderate, 4 = strong, 5 = near-certain copy-paste artefact.
scoring.minMatches: Rule only counts once it fires at least this many times in the whole text (stops a single em dash or "crucial" condemning a message).
scoring.suggestion: Split text into sentences. For each sentence, sum the weights of matching rules (cap at ~8), add statistical signals at document level, then map to a 0–100 AI score with something like 1 - exp(-score/4). Highlight matched spans in the AI colour. Any weight-5 hit can force a high minimum score.
scoring.caveat: These are style tells, not proof. Formal writers, non-native speakers, and people who’ve picked up AI habits will trigger some of them. Show the reasons, not just the number.

rules.label: Non-breaking hyphen (U+2011)
rules.description: ChatGPT often writes hyphenated words with U+2011 instead of a normal hyphen. Looks identical, almost never typed by a person.

rules.label: Narrow no-break space (U+202F)
rules.description: Used between numbers and units/% by some models ("15 %"). Invisible to the eye.

rules.label: Zero-width characters
rules.description: Zero-width space/joiner/BOM characters left in copied output.

rules.label: Non-breaking space (U+00A0)
rules.description: Regular-looking space that is actually NBSP. Common in copied AI/web output.

rules.label: Thin/hair space
rules.description: Typographic spaces (U+2009/U+200A) people don’t type.

rules.label: Em dash (—)
rules.description: The classic tell. Heavier when there are several, or when spaced " — " in casual text like Slack.

rules.label: Spaced en dash used as a dash
rules.description: En dash with spaces either side used like an em dash.

rules.label: Arrows in prose
rules.description: "X → Y" shorthand for flows/causation.

rules.label: Single ellipsis character (…)
rules.description: One-glyph ellipsis rather than three dots. Weak: phones auto-convert.

rules.label: Curly quotes / apostrophes
rules.description: Smart quotes. Weak on its own (Mac/iOS/Word insert them) but a real tell in Slack, which does not curl quotes.

rules.label: Multiplication sign (×)
rules.description: "3× faster" using the real × glyph instead of x.

rules.label: Hyphenated plural durations ("15-years")
rules.description: Hyphen joining a number to a plural unit, e.g. "15-years of experience", "3-months". Correct is "15 years" or "15-year-old".

rules.label: Buzzword compound adjectives
rules.description: Stacked hyphenated marketing adjectives.

rules.label: Emoji used as bullets / line starts
rules.description: Lines starting with ✅ 🚀 💡 📌 🔥 ✨ etc. LinkedIn/ChatGPT style.

rules.label: Markdown bold left in text (**like this**)
rules.description: Raw markdown pasted into a place that does not render it.

rules.label: Markdown headings (### Heading)
rules.description: Raw markdown heading syntax.

rules.label: Markdown horizontal rule (---)
rules.description: Section dividers on their own line.

rules.label: Bold lead-in bullets (**Thing:** detail)
rules.description: Bullets or lines that open with a bolded label, then a colon/full stop, then the explanation.
rules.example: - **Speed:** It loads in under a second.

rules.label: Label lead-in bullets (Thing. detail / Thing: detail)
rules.description: Same pattern after formatting is stripped: short Capitalised label (1–5 words) + "." or ":" then a sentence. Needs 2+ in a text.
rules.example: - Speed. It loads in under a second.

rules.label: Title Case heading lines
rules.description: Short standalone lines In Title Case (optionally ending with a colon).

rules.label: Template placeholders
rules.description: [Your Name], [Company], [Insert date] left in.

rules.label: Chatbot citation / tracking artefacts
rules.description: Definitive copy-paste leftovers: 【source】 markers, turn0search0, oaicite, utm_source=chatgpt.com etc.

rules.label: AI self-reference / cutoff talk
rules.description: "As an AI language model", "as of my last update", etc.
rules.pattern: \bas an AI(?: language model| assistant)?\b|\bI['’]?m (?:just )?an AI\b|\bas of my (?:last|latest) (?:update|knowledge|training)|\bknowledge cut-?off\b|\bI (?:don['’]t|do not) have (?:access to )?(?:real[- ]time|personal (?:opinions|experiences|feelings))
rules.example: As an AI language model, I cannot

rules.label: "It’s not X, it’s Y" (negative parallelism)
rules.description: Reframing contrast: "It’s not about speed — it’s about trust." One of the strongest stylistic tells.
rules.pattern: \b(?:it['’]?s|this is|that['’]?s|it is|this isn['’]t|it isn['’]t|that isn['’]t)\s+(?:not\s+)?(?:just\s+|only\s+|merely\s+|really\s+)?(?:about\s+)?[^.;\n]{1,60}?(?:[,;—–]|\s-\s|\.)\s*(?:it['’]?s|it is|this is|that['’]?s|but)\b
rules.example: It’s not about speed — it’s about trust.
rules.note: Broad. For precision, require "not"/"isn’t" in the match (filter in code).

rules.label: "Not just X, but Y"
rules.description: Not just/only/merely … but (also) …
rules.example: not just a tool, but a partner

rules.label: "No X. No Y. Just Z."
rules.description: Stacked negation fragments.
rules.example: No fluff. No jargon. Just results.

rules.label: Three one-word sentences ("Simple. Fast. Reliable.")
rules.description: Punchy single-word fragments in a row.

rules.label: Rhetorical question then reveal ("The result? …")
rules.description: Self-answered mini questions used for drama.
rules.pattern: \b(?:The (?:result|answer|catch|kicker|twist|best part|problem|reason|truth|secret|difference|key|takeaway|upshot|outcome|fix|goal|impact)|Why does (?:this|it|that) matter|What changed|The real question|And honestly|Honestly|Why)\?(?=\s|$)

rules.label: "Here’s the thing / Here’s why / Here’s what…"
rules.description: Set-up phrases that announce what’s coming.
rules.example: Here’s the thing: nobody reads docs.

rules.label: Rule of three lists
rules.description: "X, Y, and Z" triads. Weak alone; counts when frequent.

rules.label: Trailing "-ing" significance clause
rules.description: ", highlighting / underscoring / ensuring / showcasing …" tacked on the end to add fake depth.
rules.example: The team shipped early, highlighting their commitment.

rules.label: "Whether you’re X or Y, …"
rules.description: Audience-spanning opener.
rules.example: Whether you’re a beginner or a pro,

rules.label: "From X to Y, …" range opener
rules.description: False-range framing at the start of a sentence.
rules.example: From onboarding to checkout, every step

rules.label: Label-colon sentence starts
rules.description: "Quick note:", "Pro tip:", "Spoiler:", "Hot take:", "Short answer:" etc.
rules.pattern: (?:^|[.!?]\s+)(?:Quick note|Pro tip|Spoiler|Hot take|Short answer|Long answer|Short version|TL;?DR|Bottom line|The bottom line|Key takeaways?|In short|The upshot|Reality check|Translation|Next steps?)\s*:

rules.label: Chatbot openers
rules.description: "Great question!", "Certainly!", "Absolutely!", "Sure! Here’s…", "I’d be happy to…"
rules.pattern: (?:^|\n)\s*(?:Great question|Good question|What a great question|Certainly|Absolutely|Of course|Sure[!,]\s*[Hh]ere|I['’]?d be (?:happy|glad|delighted) to|Happy to help|Okay,? here['’]s|Got it[!.,]|You['’]re (?:absolutely|completely|totally) right|Great point|Love this)

rules.label: Offer-to-do-more closers
rules.description: "Let me know if you’d like…", "Want me to…?", "If you’d like, I can…", "Hope this helps!"
rules.pattern: \b(?:Let me know if (?:you['’]?d like|you want|you need|that helps|anything)|Feel free to (?:let me know|reach out|ask|adjust|tweak)|I hope (?:this|that) helps|Hope (?:this|that) helps|Would you like me to|Do you want me to|Want me to\b|If you['’]?d? (?:like|want),? I (?:can|could)|Happy to (?:adjust|tweak|expand|refine|dig|help|elaborate))
rules.example: Want me to turn this into a table?

rules.label: Wrap-up signposts
rules.description: "In summary", "In conclusion", "Overall,", "Ultimately,", "All in all"
rules.pattern: (?:^|[.!?]\s+)(?:In (?:summary|conclusion|essence|a nutshell)|Overall,|Ultimately,|To (?:summari[sz]e|sum up|wrap up|conclude)|All in all|At the end of the day)

rules.label: Formal transition starters
rules.description: Sentences opening with Moreover / Furthermore / Additionally / Notably / Importantly…

rules.label: Email clichés
rules.description: "I hope this email finds you well", "Please don’t hesitate to…", "I wanted to reach out"
rules.pattern: \bI hope (?:this|my) (?:email|message|note) finds you well|\bPlease (?:don['’]t|do not) hesitate to\b|\bI wanted to (?:reach out|follow up|touch base)\b|\bThank you for reaching out\b|\bI trust this (?:email|message) finds you\b
rules.example: I hope this email finds you well.

rules.label: LinkedIn-style hooks
rules.description: "Let that sink in.", "Read that again.", "And that’s okay.", "This is huge."
rules.pattern: \b(?:Let that sink in|Read that again|And that['’]s okay|This is huge|Here['’]s what I learned|I['’]m thrilled to (?:announce|share)|I['’]m humbled|Agree\?|Thoughts\?\s*$)

rules.label: "It’s worth noting / It’s important to note"
rules.description: Throat-clearing hedges.
rules.pattern: \b(?:it['’]?s|it is) (?:worth (?:noting|mentioning|highlighting)|important to (?:note|remember|understand|recogni[sz]e|consider)|crucial to|essential to)\b|\bIt should be noted\b|\bKeep in mind that\b

rules.label: "plays a crucial role" & friends
rules.description: Plays a crucial/vital/pivotal/key role; serves as; stands as; a testament to.
rules.pattern: \bplays? an? (?:crucial|vital|pivotal|key|significant|central|critical|integral) role\b|\b(?:serves|stands|acts) as an? (?:testament|reminder|cornerstone|catalyst|beacon|bridge)\b|\ba testament to\b|\bmarks? a (?:pivotal|significant|major) (?:moment|milestone|shift|step)\b
rules.example: plays a crucial role in growth

rules.label: "Let’s dive in / break it down / unpack"
rules.description: Tour-guide verbs.

rules.label: Stock AI phrases
rules.description: In today’s fast-paced world, ever-evolving landscape, rich tapestry, unlock the potential, navigate the complexities, a myriad of, the realm of, game changer, next level, harness the power…
rules.pattern: \bin today['’]s (?:fast-paced|digital|ever-changing|rapidly evolving|modern|competitive) (?:world|landscape|age|era|environment)\b|\bever-(?:evolving|changing) (?:world|landscape)\b|\b(?:rich|vibrant|intricate) tapestry\b|\bunlock(?:ing)? (?:the |its |your )?(?:full )?potential\b|\bnavigat(?:e|ing) the (?:complexities|challenges|intricacies|landscape)\b|\ba (?:myriad|plethora) of\b|\bin the (?:realm|world) of\b|\bgame[- ]changer\b|\bto the next level\b|\bharness(?:ing)? the power\b|\bthe power of\b|\bat its core\b|\bthe heart of\b|\bembark(?:ing)? on (?:a|this|your) journey\b|\bseamless(?:ly)? integrat\w*|\bfast-paced\b|\bshed(?:s|ding)? light on\b|\bstrike a balance\b|\bpave the way\b|\bremains to be seen\b
rules.example: In today’s fast-paced world, we must unlock our potential

rules.label: Over-used AI vocabulary
rules.description: delve, tapestry, testament, landscape, realm, leverage, robust, seamless, pivotal, crucial, vibrant, multifaceted, intricate, nuanced, holistic, foster, underscore, showcase, elevate, empower, streamline, unlock, harness, embark, beacon, bustling, meticulous, commendable, paramount, synergy, resonate, unwavering, interplay, endeavour, invaluable, transformative, boasts, garner, bolster, enhance, comprehensive, notably. One hit means little; density matters.
rules.example: We leverage robust, seamless tooling to foster growth

rules.label: Sincerity intensifiers
rules.description: genuinely, truly, incredibly, honestly, deeply, absolutely — sprinkled for warmth.

rules.label: Doubled adjectives
rules.description: Stock pairs: clear and concise, safe and secure, fast and reliable, simple and intuitive…
rules.pattern: \b(?:clear and concise|safe and secure|fast and reliable|simple and intuitive|clean and modern|robust and scalable|efficient and effective|timely and accurate|engaging and informative|seamless and intuitive)\b

rules.label: American spellings (opt-in)
rules.description: AI defaults to US English. Only useful if the author normally writes British English (e.g. UK colleagues).

statisticalSignals.label: Low sentence-length variation
statisticalSignals.description: Humans mix very short and very long sentences; AI keeps them similar. Compute the coefficient of variation (stdev / mean) of words per sentence.
statisticalSignals.heuristic: CV < 0.35 → AI-leaning; CV > 0.6 → human-leaning. Needs ~5+ sentences.

statisticalSignals.label: Uniform paragraph / bullet lengths
statisticalSignals.description: Every paragraph or bullet roughly the same size.
statisticalSignals.heuristic: CV of words per paragraph (or per bullet) < 0.3 with 3+ blocks.

statisticalSignals.label: No casual markers (in chat contexts)
statisticalSignals.description: Slack-style human text has lowercase starts, "i", missing full stops, typos, "lol", "tbh", "imo", "fwiw", repeated letters.
statisticalSignals.heuristic: Zero lowercase sentence starts, zero informal tokens and perfect terminal punctuation across 4+ sentences → nudge AI.

statisticalSignals.label: Contraction balance
statisticalSignals.description: Older/formal models avoid contractions entirely; humans in chat use lots.
statisticalSignals.heuristic: Contractions per 100 words < 0.5 in casual text → nudge AI.

statisticalSignals.label: High list / heading density
statisticalSignals.description: Large share of lines are bullets or headings in what should be a chat message.
statisticalSignals.heuristic: > 40% of lines are bullets/headings in a message under 300 words.

statisticalSignals.label: Moderate, even lexical diversity
statisticalSignals.description: AI text tends to sit in a narrow type-token band and reuses connective words.
statisticalSignals.heuristic: Use MATTR (moving-average type-token ratio, window 50). Treat as a weak tiebreaker only.

statisticalSignals.label: Low perplexity (optional, needs a local model)
statisticalSignals.description: Text a small language model finds very predictable is more likely generated. Could run a tiny local model (e.g. via llama.cpp) per sentence.
statisticalSignals.heuristic: Rank sentences by perplexity within the text; lowest-perplexity spans get an AI bump.
